summary: Dashboard sparklines show stale/partial data after account-level analytics retention policy change
description: Issue summary: After BrightGrid updated their account-level analytics retention from 90d -> 30d on 2026-03-09, several dashboard sparklines and usage charts began showing flat or missing data for the last 7 days for that tenant. Impact: Customer-facing dashboards under Console show stale metrics (flat lines) for token usage, per-route latency percentiles, and streaming counts. This affects product analytics and billing reconciliation for the customer. Environment: prod (us-east), BrightGrid tenant ID: bg-1974. Steps to reproduce: 1) Log into Console as BrightGrid admin > Metrics > Usage dashboard. 2) Set time range to Last 7 days. 3) Observe sparklines and per-minute charts for token usage show flat lines after 2026-03-09. 4) Set time range to Last 90 days -> historical data beyond 30d shows correctly. Expected behavior: Sparklines should display incremental per-minute/per-hour metrics across the requested time window. Actual behavior: Recent data points (post retention change) are missing or collapsed to zero. Recent raw logs and model traffic still show requests served. Logs/observations: - retention-worker logs (2026-03-09 02:15 UTC) show repeated "checkpoint timeout" and "partial-shard prune" messages for tenant bg-1974. - analytics-service returned 500 on aggregation job: "Failed to materialize timeseries slice (timeout)". - Console UI requests for /api/metrics/series returned HTTP 200 with empty series payload in several traces. Initial customer message: "After changing retention our console graphs are gone for last week — billing is wrong and we need immediate help."
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged. Opening investigation and assigning to infra. Sharing preliminary troubleshooting steps and asking for a short list of affected dashboards.

2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE (Priya Nair): Seeing retention-worker timeouts for bg-1974. Job ID rw-job-33214 timed out when processing large metric shard; fallback removed partial aggregation keys. Investigating whether pruning logic removed active windows.

2026-03-10 11:22 - Customer (Samira Khan, BrightGrid): Confirmed the affected dashboards are: Token Usage (per-route), Streaming Connections, and Generation Latency. We have spikes around 2026-03-08 to 03-09 that matter for billing.

2026-03-11 02:47 - Eng (Miguel Torres): Ran backfill query to re-aggregate raw events for bg-1974 for 2026-03-06 -> 2026-03-10. Partial success; reprocessed ~82% of windows before we hit a different rate limit. Preparing an incremental backfill with checkpointing.

2026-03-12 14:10 - Support (Aisha Patel): Communicated planned workaround to customer: manual incremental backfill and short-term retention-worker config tune. Customer accepted and requested ETA for full restoration.

2026-03-13 07:35 - Eng (Miguel Torres): Hotfix deployed to retention-worker (commit redwood/retention-worker@a7f3b2) to add checkpoint and shard-throttle behavior. Triggered controlled backfill; monitoring shows charts repopulating for last 72 hours.
investigation: Hypothesis: A retention policy change triggered an immediate prune run that attempted to compact multiple metric shards for the tenant. The retention-worker v2.3.4 pruning path lacks proper checkpointing for large shards and cancels aggregation mid-flight, which can leave time-series windows un-materialized. Queries executed: 1) SELECT count(*) FROM raw_events WHERE tenant='bg-1974' AND ts >= '2026-03-06' GROUP BY minute — raw events present. 2) Job logs inspected in S3: rw-job-33214 shows repeated timeouts and HTTP 500s from analytics-service v2.3.4 for aggregation slices. Observed symptoms: - Empty series responses from /api/metrics/series for 1-minute resolution requests. - Backfill attempts hit internal per-tenant rate limiter before completion. - No signs of data deletion from raw_events store; issue localized to aggregation/materialization layer. Links: dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/tenants/bg-1974/metrics, logs: s3://redwood-logs/rw-job-33214, PR reference redwood/retention-worker#128.
resolution: Workaround applied: Ran an incremental backfill job with checkpointing for bg-1974 to re-materialize missing windows; throttled backfill to stay under per-tenant rate limits. Hotfix: Deployed retention-worker patch (redwood/retention-worker@a7f3b2) that implements shard-level checkpoints and exponential retry for aggregation slices. Also bumped analytics-service aggregation timeout from 30s -> 90s for the short term while backfills complete. Result: charts repopulated for the last 72 hours within 3 hours of the hotfix, and full 7-day repopulation reached ~99% after controlled backfills. Follow-up actions: - Create a postmortem (INT-1409) to analyze retention pruning behavior and prevent eager prune on policy change. - Add automated alert if retention-worker prunes more than X% of a tenant's active windows in a single run. - Add canary to retention config changes to avoid global immediate prune (tracked in redwood/console-ui#402). Related PRs/commits: redwood/retention-worker#128 (hotfix), redwood/console-ui#402 (UI guardrails).
notes: Customer notified on 2026-03-13 09:00 UTC: issue mostly resolved; support provided ticket summary and next steps for audits.
